newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria mulls barter grain deal with Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria mulls barter grain deal with Kazakhstan.

text.p: Bulgaria, hit by a severe grain shortage, is negotiating to import wheat from Kazakhstan in a barter deal, an agriculture ministry official said.

"Ministry officials are now negotiating with a visiting Kazakh delegation," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters. She said several different barter options were being considered but gave no more details.
High wheat exports in 1995 and a record low yield this year due to poor weather and lack of fertilisers have triggered serious bread shortages in this traditionally agricultural country.
The official said Bulgaria was looking at barter deals because it was short of cash.
Bulgaria's current wheat supplies stand at 130,000 tonnes, while domestic wheat consumption is 500,000 tonnes a year, the agricultural ministry has said.

Last week, Bulgaria lost a $25 million credit guarantee for the import of 120,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat after state-owned Bulbank refused to confirm the credit line, saying the conditions were unfavourable.
